findings.evidence: DOM order: step with order:3 (Confirm your order) appears first, step with order:2 (Enter payment details) second, step with order:1 (Choose a plan) third. CSS order property reverses this to 1, 2, 3 visually.
findings.violation: DOM order does not preserve the meaningful sequence. Screen reader users and those with CSS disabled encounter steps in the reverse of the intended task sequence: Confirm before Choose.
findings.fix: Remove the order CSS property and reorder the DOM elements so they appear as Choose a plan, Enter payment details, Confirm your order in both DOM and visual order.

findings.evidence: Element is a div with class icon-delete containing an img with empty alt text. No role attribute, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, no accessible text content.
findings.violation: Custom control exposes no programmatic name, role, or state. Screen reader users cannot detect this control exists or determine what it does.
findings.fix: Add role=button and aria-label=Delete to the div, implement keyboard handlers (Enter and Space keys) to activate it, and ensure focus management when activated.

findings.evidence: Input id=promo has aria-invalid=true. Associated error text reads only Error. with no description of what validation failed or how to correct it.
findings.violation: Error message is generic and does not describe the problem. User cannot determine what to fix to resolve the validation failure.
findings.fix: Replace Error. with a specific message that identifies the field (if not already clear from context) and describes the validation rule that failed, e.g., Promo code must be 6-10 alphanumeric characters.

findings.evidence: Page provides one navigation mechanism: primary navigation menu at top (Plan a trip, Service alerts). Footer links (Privacy policy, Terms of service) are utility links, not page-location aids. No search, sitemap, or breadcrumb trail present.
findings.violation: Fewer than two independent mechanisms exist to locate this page from within the site. Users arriving from search results have limited navigation options.
findings.fix: Add at least one more navigation mechanism independent of the primary menu, such as a site search feature, a breadcrumb trail showing the page's position in the information hierarchy, or a related-pages list.
